card.name: Words just before 'packed with' or 'full of'
card.fires_on: The word right before an expected 'packed with', 'loaded with' or 'chock-full of' phrase, usually a verb like are/is or a noun that is about to be described as full of good things. It appears in promotional or descriptive web text.

modes.label: Verb before 'packed with'
modes.description: Is/are after a subject such as foods, where 'packed with nutrients' is likely next.
modes.example: After all, each of these foods<< is>> packed with nutrients, light on calories,

modes.label: Part of 'chock-full'
modes.description: The start of an unusual word like chock-full or lousy, meaning full of something.
modes.example: So You Want to Be President? is<< ch>>ock-full of interesting tidbits about our

modes.label: Noun that holds many things
modes.description: A noun such as area, issue or year that is about to be described as rich in content.
modes.example: Each monthly<< issue>> includes expert science reporting, vivid color photography

card.writes: It pushes the model to continue with 'packed', 'packing' or 'pack' words.
card.plain: It fires where the text is about to say something is packed with or full of good content.
